clue.text: Lack support where game is involved

indicators.note: the game is involved in, wrapped inside, the word for support

parts.note: a shore is a prop or beam holding something up
tag is the playground chasing game

explanation.surface: A complaint that a sport lacks backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved' is the container signal; 'support' reads as backing, but here it is a prop or beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall or want of something is a lack of it; both nouns name a deficiency.

clue.text: Give way to founder

explanation.surface: Collapsing to whoever started the business.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way; to founder is to collapse or fail, also yielding to pressure.

clue.text: Junior dogsbody.. out of condition, sweet child!

parts.note: food gone bad is off, no longer in good condition
an ice is an ice cream or water ice, a sweet
a boy is a male child

explanation.surface: An unfit errand boy and a darling child.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a dogsbody is someone who does menial chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad employed to run errands and do menial tasks in an office.

clue.text: Carrying piano, pulls a muscle

indicators.note: the word for pulls carries the letter inside it

parts.note: to trice is a sailing term for hauling up with a rope
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Lugging a piano, someone strains their arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' is the container signal. To trice (up) is an old nautical verb for hoisting with a rope, so 'pulls' is a verb, not a noun about muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: It could give out bang

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could give, be rearranged into, the answer

explanation.surface: Something that might go off with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could give' rearranges OUT BANG; the whole clue also describes the answer, a warship that fires guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A small armed vessel fires its guns, sending out bangs.

clue.text: Zone in which glider crashed

indicators.note: a crashed glider is wrecked, so its letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An area where a glider came down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges the six letters of GLIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt or band encircling something is a zone, the old sense of the word (as in torrid zone).

clue.text: District Commissioner in Lagos to represent the old country

indicators.note: the commissioner's letters go in the rearranged letters
to represent is to re-present, so the letters of the city and the word to are set out anew

parts.note: DC is the abbreviation for District Commissioner, a colonial official

explanation.surface: A colonial official in Nigeria standing for an old West African territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represent' is the anagram signal for LAGOS plus TO, and 'in' places DC within. The Gold Coast is the old colonial name of Ghana; Lagos itself is in Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gold Coast was the colonial name of what became Ghana, a former British territory.

clue.text: A climber might carry it, having climbed with a friend

parts.note: rose is the past of rise, meaning climbed
bud is American slang for a friend, short for buddy

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's mascot, carried on a climb with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A climber' is not a mountaineer but a climbing plant, a rambling rose that bears the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose bears unopened flower heads on its stems.

clue.text: A charge may be put on this pastille

definitions.text: A charge may be put on this

explanation.surface: A sweet that someone might be billed for.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the diamond shape is a field on which charges (emblems) are borne; a pastille is a medicated sweet of that shape.

clue.text: Century of Scandinavian trouble and fag

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
taken as written
a Finn is a native of Finland, loosely counted among Scandinavians
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A Nordic person's hundred woes, plus a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a fag is a cigarette; the compound is old slang for a cigarette, as each one supposedly hastens the smoker's burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang name for a cigarette, from the idea that smoking hastens the grave.

clue.text: The extent of loud moans

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for moans is heard as a different word

parts.note: sighs are low moans of sorrow or weariness

explanation.surface: Someone measuring how much noisy groaning there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud' tells you SIGHS is spoken, giving a word of the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is dimension or magnitude, how far something extends.

clue.text: Novel can combine lust with corruption

indicators.note: corruption spoils and distorts, so the letters of these three words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a book can mix desire with depravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruption' rearranges the fourteen letters of CAN COMBINE LUST into the title of Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe's 1852 book is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Act in loco parentis by leading son into temptation

indicators.note: the pair of pieces is put into the word for temptation

parts.note: bait is a lure or enticement

indicators.note: by goes ahead of son, leading it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent figure leads a boy astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' and 'into' are the signals; in loco parentis is Latin for in the place of a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding a child while the parents are out means standing in for them, the Latin phrase's meaning.

clue.text: Where water can be found generally

explanation.surface: A question about where water usually is.
explanation.definitionFit: Water runs in the mains supply pipe; the phrase also means for the most part, on the whole.

clue.text: About to finish, the players passed to and fro

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, players

indicators.note: about here means turned around, mixed, so the word for finishing is rearranged

parts.note: to die is to come to an end, to finish

explanation.surface: The musicians kept passing something back and forth as the set neared its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is the anagram signal, giving IED. 'About to finish' reads as one phrase meaning nearly done, but it splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or remarks bandied about are tossed back and forth between people.

clue.text: Unreadable articles from abroad about Rock

indicators.note: the foreign articles go about, around, the name for the Rock

parts.note: il and le are definite articles in Italian and French, le doubling up here
Gib is short for Gibraltar, known as the Rock

explanation.surface: Foreign newspaper pieces about Gibraltar that nobody can make out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. Gibraltar, a British territory at the tip of Spain, is nicknamed the Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting too poor to decipher is not legible, unreadable.

clue.text: Payment for prince, perhaps

explanation.surface: Wondering what fee to pay a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalty is a fee paid to an author or patent holder; collectively, royalty is the royal family, a prince being one.

clue.text: A capital show place

explanation.surface: A city that puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state capital of Washington, USA, and also the London exhibition hall that hosts trade shows.

clue.text: There are no limits to the obloquy heaped upon us, old boy

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece is heaped on top of the other
no limits means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: calumny is slander or abuse, obloquy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old pupil complains of endless abuse piled on his classmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There are no limits to' strips C and Y from CALUMNY, leaving ALUMN, and 'heaped upon' sets it above US in the down light. Old boy is British for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A former pupil of a school or college is a graduate of it.

clue.text: Fluff rattles young actress

indicators.note: to fluff is to bungle, so the letters of rattles are botched into another order

explanation.surface: A nervous young actress keeps fluffing her lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' looks like a noun but is a verb meaning to botch, and it rearranges RATTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a promising young film actress on the way to stardom.

clue.text: To make a saving, learned to accept a perk

indicators.note: the word for learned takes the perk inside it

parts.note: a sage is wise or learned
LV is a luncheon voucher, a staff perk in Britain

explanation.surface: A thrifty scholar taking a fringe benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' is the container signal. Luncheon vouchers (LVs) were meal coupons given to British employees as a perk.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue goods from loss or wreck is to save them, a saving.

clue.text: Girl gives song a rousing finish

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: rousing means rising, so the word for finish reads upwards in this down light

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: A girl sings a song with a stirring climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rousing' turns END upwards to DNE. Ariadne is the girl in Greek myth who helped Theseus escape the labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne is a woman's name, from the Cretan princess of myth.

clue.text: House covered in the finest heat-resistant tiles

indicators.note: the answer is covered in, concealed within, the run of these words

explanation.surface: Heat-proof tiles of the best quality on a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' gives the answer from finesT HEAT-REsistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is a playhouse; a full audience is a good house.

clue.text: I know that I'm a confidant

explanation.surface: Someone claims to know they are being trusted with secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of emphatic agreement; read literally it says the speaker is the one being confided in.

clue.text: Making a turn, goes smartly in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means the word for going smartly is read backwards

parts.note: to nip is to go quickly, as in nip to the shops

explanation.surface: A car turning round by quickly backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns NIPS around. The definition reads as the answer in its verb sense, to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate rapidly is to whirl round, which is making a turn.

clue.text: Help princess to fish, catching a flounder

parts.note: Aida is the Ethiopian princess of Verdi's opera

indicators.note: the word for fishing catches, holds inside, the flatfish

parts.note: to net is to fish with a net
a dab is a kind of flounder, a small flatfish

explanation.surface: A royal goes fishing and lands a flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' is the container signal. 'flounder' looks like a verb meaning struggle, but here it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase means to assist, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Endlessly cultivating fruit

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: raising crops is cultivating them

explanation.surface: Someone forever tending fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last letter, G, from RAISING.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a dried fruit.

clue.text: Swiss girl's embraced by boy

indicators.note: the girl's name is embraced, held inside, the boy's name

parts.note: Gene is a man's name
Eve's, with the possessive giving the S, is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from Switzerland in a boy's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' is the container signal; 'Swiss' looks like part of the girl's description but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevese describes a native of Geneva, a Swiss city.
